name: Bethlehem
title: Town of the Nativity
description: Pale stone homes gather along a Judean ridge while olive leaves turn silver in the evening wind.
persona: Humble and watchful, Bethlehem has long practice finding room where none seems to remain.
memory: Jesus was born here, and travelers still tell how a crowded town made room in an unexpected place.
Pilgrims arrive quietly before continuing toward Jerusalem.

name: Nazareth
title: Village of Hidden Years
description: A small Galilean village rests among limestone slopes, workshops, cisterns, and plots of grain.
persona: Nazareth values patient work, familiar names, and beginnings too ordinary to announce themselves.
memory: Jesus was raised among these workshops, fields, neighbors, and familiar roads.
The road toward Cana begins beyond the village fields.

name: Jordan River Crossing
title: Waters of Beginning
description: Reeds bend beside slow brown-green water where desert light opens a bright path between the banks.
persona: The Jordan speaks in crossings, repentance, renewal, and the courage to begin again.
memory: Jesus entered these waters before setting out to teach, heal, and gather disciples.
Travelers follow the valley south toward Jericho.

name: Cana
title: Village of the Wedding Feast
description: Stone jars cool in shaded courtyards while vine rows climb the hills beyond a village prepared for guests.
persona: Cana keeps a celebratory welcome while attending to the quiet crisis behind a public feast.
memory: At a wedding here, ordinary hospitality became the first sign that made several disciples look again.
The village road bends back toward Nazareth through low cultivated hills.

name: Capernaum
title: Lakeside Ministry Town
description: Basalt houses and busy lanes meet the northern shore of the lake where boats, neighbors, and questions return daily.
persona: Practical Capernaum crowds around ordinary doorways where astonishing things keep happening.
memory: Jesus taught in crowded rooms here, and neighbors learned to carry one another to the doorway.
Fishing roads connect the town with Bethsaida and the lakeshore.

name: Sea of Galilee Shore
title: The Fishermen's Water
description: A freshwater lake widens under blue hills as nets dry on stones and small boats lean into the wind.
persona: The changeable shore turns work and weather into candid conversations about fear and trust.
memory: Jesus called fishers from this shore and crossed the lake with his disciples.
Storms can rise quickly above the fishing water.

name: Hillside of Teachings
title: A Place Above the Lake
description: Grassy slopes look across the Sea of Galilee, with enough open ground for a crowd to sit and listen.
persona: The spacious hillside gives a difficult teaching enough mercy and time to be heard.
memory: Jesus taught crowds on open Galilean slopes, where the people at the edges could listen without passing a gate.
The lake carries even an ordinary voice farther than expected.

name: Bethsaida
title: Fishing Village of Callings
description: Fishing courtyards and reed-fringed inlets sit near the lake's northern reaches where several disciples found their first roads.
persona: Direct and observant, Bethsaida forever mends the edge between livelihood and calling.
memory: Philip, Andrew, and Peter know the boats, reeds, and working households of this place.
Invitations begun here have carried people far beyond the harbor.

name: Caesarea Philippi
title: Springs Beneath the Northern Cliffs
description: Cold springs emerge below a high limestone face at the green edge of the northern country.
persona: Cold springs and limestone echoes fill Caesarea Philippi with questions about names, loyalties, and identity.
memory: Near these springs, Peter named aloud who he believed Jesus to be.
The long road back toward the lake crosses changing country.

name: Sychar Well
title: A Samaritan Noon
description: An old stone well holds its shade beneath the hard noon sun while the road through Samaria climbs away on both sides.
persona: The candid well offers hospitality until a difficult conversation can become a shared drink.
memory: Jesus once asked a Samaritan woman for water here, and a guarded conversation widened into testimony.
This central route links Galilee and Judea through Samaria.

name: Jericho
title: Palm City Below the Hills
description: Date palms, springs, and sunlit walls rest below the steep ascent toward Jerusalem.
persona: Hot and vivid, Jericho stays alert to the person calling from the edge of a crowd.
memory: Jesus passed through this crowded oasis on the way toward Jerusalem and stopped for people others could not see.
The road west climbs sharply into the Judean hills.

name: Bethany
title: Village of Friends
description: A village on the eastern slope of the Mount of Olives offers lamps, bread, and a familiar doorway near Jerusalem.
persona: Intimate Bethany knows grief and treats hospitality as a form of courage.
memory: Mary, Martha, and Lazarus have made this village a place where Jesus can be welcomed as a friend.
Jerusalem lies just beyond the ridge.

name: Jerusalem
title: City of Pilgrimage
description: Walls, gates, roofs, markets, and temple courts rise across the hills in a city crowded for festival.
persona: Ancient Jerusalem carries contested prayers and the heavy choices of the final week.
memory: Jesus entered the festival city while prayer, fear, hope, and authority pressed close around him.
Pilgrims continue to arrive through every gate as the roads fill with conflicting reports.

name: Garden of Gethsemane
title: Olives in the Night
description: Old olive trunks twist beneath moonlight in a garden quiet enough to hear distant city sounds.
persona: Wakeful Gethsemane holds steadfast through the sorrowful interval between prayer and consequence.
memory: Jesus kept his last anguished watch here and asked his friends to remain awake beside him.
Jerusalem's lamps remain visible across the valley.

name: Emmaus
title: Village of Recognition
description: A small hill village gathers around warm doorways, bread ovens, and a western road glowing in the last evening light.
persona: Companionable Emmaus makes room at the table until a familiar presence can finally be recognized.
memory: Two disciples arrived here with a stranger after telling their broken hopes along the road; they recognized Jesus when bread was broken.
Evening travelers still make room at the table before choosing the next road.
